<details class="rollup-box section-rec" id="rec-parlays">
<summary>🎟️ Parlays &amp; round robins — 8 tickets</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

Each ticket opens to show what it is, why it's on the card, and every leg.

💡 **"(est.)" price:** each leg's odds multiplied together, the standard way to estimate what a parlay pays. The book's actual payout can differ a little, and same-game parlays (several legs from one game) pay noticeably less because the legs are related. Check the payout on your slip.

<div class="rollup-controls">
  <button class="btn-toggle btn-primary" onclick="toggleRollups('section-tickets', true)">Open all tickets</button>
  <button class="btn-toggle" onclick="toggleRollups('section-tickets', false)">Close all tickets</button>

<a id="night-cap-howto"></a>
<details class="rollup-box section-tickets" id="night-cap-explainer">
<summary>🛡️ How the night-game hedge works (read this first)</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

- **Why the last leg is a night game.** These parlays end with the moneyline favorite in the Sunday-night (or Monday-night) game. That leg is a **placeholder**: it keeps the ticket alive until night so that, if the morning and afternoon legs all win, you still have a decision to make.
- **Locking in a profit.** Once only the night leg is left, bet the **underdog** in that same game. Size the bet so you come out ahead whichever team wins: if the favorite wins, the parlay pays; if the underdog wins, the hedge pays. Each ticket below shows the stake and the profit it locks at today's prices.
- **Finding a middle.** Instead of the underdog moneyline, you can hedge with the underdog **plus the points**. If the favorite wins but by less than the spread, **both** bets win. Middles are uncommon, but they are the best outcome on these tickets. If the underdog wins outright, the hedge still covers you.
- **What it costs.** The hedge is a bigger second bet, often ten times the parlay stake, and prices will have moved by the night game, so recalculate first. Hedging part of the way is fine if you want to keep some upside.
- **The formula.** Hedge stake = what the parlay pays back (stake included) ÷ the hedge bet's decimal odds. Profit locked = parlay payback − parlay stake − hedge stake.

</div>

<summary>📖 How the stars work</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

- **Stars show how much evidence lines up behind a bet**, compared with our other bets this week. More stars = a stronger case. They are **not** a win percentage.
- **Where a bet starts:** ★★★½ when our own matchup numbers **and** at least two named experts back it · ★★★ when our matchup numbers back it · ★★½ when at least two named experts picked it · ★★ when the support is only partial.
- **Up half a star** when the experts are lopsided in its favor (at least four of them, two-to-one or better), or when the big-money bettors are on the same side.
- **Down half a star** when more experts picked the other side, when the big money is on the other side, or when an injury or lineup question is still open.
- We do not use a computer model's win percentage here: ours failed its accuracy test, so it is left out.

<a id="teaser-matrix"></a>
## 3. Teaser Bets: 6-Point Wong Teasers

<div class="rollup-controls">
  <button class="btn-toggle btn-primary" onclick="toggleRollups('secmain-3', true)">Expand Section 3</button>
  <button class="btn-toggle" onclick="toggleRollups('secmain-3', false)">Collapse Section 3</button>
</div>

<details class="rollup-box section-main secmain-3" id="section-3-box" open>
<summary>🔁 Section 3: Teaser Bets: 6-Point Wong Teasers</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">



**What a teaser is:** you move the point spread 6 points in your favor on every leg, in exchange for a smaller payout, and every leg must win. The "Wong" version only uses lines where those 6 points cross both **3 and 7**, the two most common NFL winning margins: favorites of −7.5 to −8.5 (teased down to −1.5 / −2.5) and underdogs of +1.5 to +2.5 (teased up to +7.5 / +8.5). Keep teasers to 2 legs.

  <button class="btn-toggle btn-primary" onclick="toggleRollups('secmain-4', true)">Expand Section 4</button>

<summary>🐶 Section 4: The Underdog Upset Ticket: The Dogs and Why</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">



**How it works:** 6 underdogs to win outright, combined into every two-team parlay — 15 combos × $1.33, **$19.95 total**. Payout by number of winners: returns (avg): 2 hit $12, 3 hit $35, 4 hit $70, 5 hit $116, 6 hit $175. Two winners does **not** turn a profit on this build; it needs three or more. Each dog is on the ticket because we think its chance of winning is better than its price implies — not because we expect all of them to win.

## 6. Game-by-Game Breakdowns: Odds, Money, Projections & the Case

<div class="rollup-controls">
  <button class="btn-toggle btn-primary" onclick="toggleRollups('secmain-6', true)">Expand Section 6</button>
  <button class="btn-toggle" onclick="toggleRollups('secmain-6', false)">Collapse Section 6</button>

<details class="rollup-box section-main secmain-6" id="section-6-box" open>
<summary>🔍 Section 6: Game-by-Game Breakdowns: Odds, Money, Projections & the Case</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">



Each game opens with a written game script, our projected final score and the reasoning behind the card lean, with links to the experts cited and the actionable props for that game. Below that: the betting lines, key context, and every pick grouped by **sides**, **totals** and **player props**.




**What the betting lines are predicting.** Every point spread and total is really a forecast. Put the two together and you get the final score the sportsbook expects; the moneylines give each team's chance of winning. Next to that is **our own projected score** (from the game write-ups in [Section 6](#section-6-box)) and **where the bets and the money are landing**, on both sides of every market.

<details class="rollup-box section-synth" id="board-defs">
<summary>📖 What each column means (plain English)</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

- **Favorite & spread:** the team expected to win and by how many points. "BUF −7" means Buffalo has to win by 8 or more for a Buffalo spread bet to cash.
- **Total points:** the combined score the sportsbook set as its over/under line.
- **Score the lines imply:** the final score the spread and total point to together. Example: total 50.5 and BUF −7 → Buffalo about 28.8, Chargers about 21.8.
- **Our projection:** Platinum Rose's own projected final: the line, adjusted for injuries, matchups, expert opinion and money moves. Not a computer-model output.
- **Win chance:** each moneyline turned into a win probability, with the sportsbook's built-in cut removed so the two sides add up to 100%.
- **Spread / Total (bets / money):** for each side, the share of bets placed and the share of dollars wagered. Example: "O 25/51 · U 75/49" means only 25% of bets are on the Over but they carry 51% of the money.
- **💰 Big-money signal:** a side where the money share beats the bet share by 15+ points — fewer, bigger bets, usually experienced ("sharp") bettors. We record **the exact line when the signal first appears**, so later builds show whether the line has moved toward or away from that side since.

</div>
</details>

<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">📖 Game script</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">In London at 06:30 PT, Washington starts Marcus Mariota with Jayden Daniels out, Terry McLaurin doubtful and Rachaad White out. Bookmaker had pulled the Mariota, McLaurin and Jacory Croskey-Merritt prop menus at its 10/03 capture, which says the book itself isn't sure what this offense looks like. Indianapolis loses Keenan Allen (out on the 10/03 ESPN feed), so the targets concentrate on Josh Downs (72+ receiving yards at −106) and Tyler Warren (54+ at −105) on a MEDIUM secondary grade against a defense allowing 6.4 yards per play. Jonathan Taylor (91+ rushing at −102) runs into the Washington run defense the WAS backers lean on, so the Colts win through the air. Indianapolis by six: a cover of −4.5 by a point and a half, 46 total points.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">🧠 Why the card leans this way</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Experts split 7–4 toward Washington: <a href="#exp-ind-was-action-network">Action Network</a> ("Mariota is a top-tier backup"), <a href="#exp-ind-was-bettingpros">BettingPros</a>, <a href="#exp-ind-was-even-money">Ross Tucker</a> and Doug Kezirian at +3.5, PFF and Travis Pulver of BettingPros on the moneyline, and Mike Florio (Commanders 24–20) on WAS; Brandon Anderson, <a href="#exp-ind-was-bettingpros">Andrew Erickson</a> and Jason Logan at −3.5 and Ian Undery of Action Network on the moneyline for IND. Dave Tuley of VSiN passes. The line has moved from the Action Network open of IND −3.5 to −4.5. Splits: WAS has 68% of spread tickets but only 58% of the money; the IND moneyline has 70% of tickets and 83% of the money, short of a 15-point sharp gap. The projection (IND by 6) disagrees with the expert majority, but only by a point and a half against the number, so the lean is to pass the side and play the receiver: Brandon Anderson and Andrew Erickson both have Downs over 62.5 receiving, noting Washington has allowed the most wide-receiver fantasy points. The projected 46 sits a point under the 47 total; The over has four backers (BettingPros and Zachary Cohen of VSiN at 46.5, Ian Undery at 49.5, and a betting-trends account on X), mostly on the same 15–1 trend when Washington is a 3.5- to 9.5-point underdog. With the projection a point under and a first-half under system in Evan Abrams' primer, no total. Card: no ticket touches this game. The projection (IND by 6) and the 7–4 expert lean to Washington point opposite ways, so the card passes the side and the receiving props.</p>

Indianapolis is −5 in turnover margin through three games, so two giveaways turn a six-point Colts win into a Washington cover. Recheck inactives at about 05:00 PT.</p>

<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">📖 Game script</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Minnesota is 3–0 because of its defense: 13.7 points allowed and a 22.7% third-down rate allowed under Brian Flores. The offense gains only 4.3 yards per play, and Justin Jefferson is out. Kyler Murray is listed active on the 10/03 feed, but Bookmaker had no Minnesota passing market at its 10/03 capture (BetOnline priced him at 183+ on Oct 2), so the QB status needs a check. Aaron Jones Sr. (−200 to score at BetOnline), Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson carry the offense. Miami is without De'Von Achane; Malik Willis (170+ passing) throws to Malik Washington (39+) and Chris Bell (35+), with Jaylen Wright (29+) in the backfield. It's a fixed-roof stadium. Minnesota by eight, so Miami covers +10; 36 points, under 38.5.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">🧠 Why the card leans this way</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">MIA: <a href="#exp-mia-min-action-network">Action Network</a> (+11), <a href="#exp-mia-min-sharp-or-square">Sharp or Square</a> (+11), Stuckey, and three more at +10.5: PJ Walsh's PRO projection, and Steve Makinen and Wes Reynolds of VSiN. MIN: Derrik Klassen (−10.5) and Mike Florio (Vikings 24–14); Dave Tuley passes. Under: Doug Kezirian of Action Network and SDQL GURU (38.5), Josh Shepardson of Sharp Football (39, a best bet), <a href="#exp-mia-min-bettingpros">Andrew Erickson</a> (39.5) and <a href="#exp-mia-min-bettingpros">BettingPros</a> (41.5). Evan Abrams' primer has two systems on Miami (fading no-pedigree favorites, and the winless-team system). There are two big-money flags on Miami: MIA +10 has 30% of tickets and 46% of the money, and the MIA moneyline has 4% of tickets and 26% of the money. The line went from the Action Network open of MIN −10.5 to −10, and the total from 42.5 to 38.5. The lean is MIA +10. The under is the right side but four points are already gone; Action Network's Evan likes Willis' rushing over as the prop. Card: Single MIA +10 ($15) is the biggest single, MIA +10 is also in the Slot 5 Hybrid, and MIA +10.5 is a proposed SuperContest pick (book +10 on both SuperContest tickets). The 7b Afternoon prop stack carries a Malik Willis interception, a deliberate partial hedge against the MIA spread.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">⚠️ What breaks it</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Minnesota's defense scores, or Willis turns it over twice under pressure from Flores, and the Vikings win by 14. If Murray doesn't start, Minnesota's offense gets even thinner, which helps the under and the Miami cover but adds noise. Recheck at the 11:35 PT inactive window.</p>

- 📈 The Broncos have come back down 10+ pts in consecutive games against Rams and Jaguars. Last decade, teams to win b2b games trailing by 10+ pts in each are just 7-13 ATS in their next game.

When San Francisco faces a non-NFC West opponent at home, they are 9-3 SU and 8-4 ATS since 2024.
- 📈 This will be Sean Payton's 11th total game as a head coach vs. 49ers. he was favored in the first ten (7-3 SU), with this being his first as an underdog.
- 📈 From strictly an on-field results standpoint, Bo Nix has been a very different QB home vs road.  Home: 17-3 SU, 14-6 ATS / 18-1-1 in a 7-pt teaser Road: 10-9 SU, 8-11 ATS / 16-3 in 7-pt teaser (2-10 ATS in his last 12 road starts)
- 📈 Nobody believes in us. Since start of 2024, Bo Nix has started 20 games where the other team was receiving majority ticket support -- Nix and the Broncos are 14-6 ATS in those games, most profitable mark for any QB in that span.

<details class="rollup-box section-main secmain-7" id="section-7-box" open>
<summary>🧭 Section 7: What the Experts Say: Consensus & Clashes</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">




**What the experts are saying, counted fairly.** We collect picks from betting podcasts, YouTube shows and betting writers, then count each source **once per game** on the side it picked most. A lopsided count (for example 6–1) means broad agreement; a **clash** means credible sources are split. The table ranks games from the strongest agreement down.

<details class="rollup-box section-3" id="consensus-defs">
<summary>📖 How to read this section</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

- **Source:** one outlet, podcast host or writer. Outlets that publish several writers (ESPN, VSiN) still count as one vote.
- **For – Against:** sources backing the consensus side vs. the other side. Ties inside one source are dropped.
- **Strength** (the table is ordered by this first): 🌟 Near-unanimous = at least 3× as many sources on one side, or none against · 🔥 Majority = ahead by 2 or more · ⚔️ Clash = ahead by only 1 · ⚖️ Split = dead even.
- **Total lean:** whether more sources picked the Over or the Under.
- **Agreement is not a guarantee.** Heavy consensus on a popular side can already be priced into the line; see the big-money column in Section 6.

[⬆ Back to Our Picks](#recommendations)
</div>
</details>

**Build rules from the season record:**

| # | Rule | Evidence (season, unique legs) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **No −120 to −100 connector legs** unless sourcing tier 1–2 (Section 4). Take −121 or longer, or plus money. | 31-45-1, 41% vs 53% needed, −23% (n=76), bad both weeks |
| 2 | **Underdog spreads are allowed when the matchup and price case are stated.** Do not use points merely to make a parlay leg feel safer. | Week 1 spread dogs were 10-20, −44%; that is a review signal, not a prohibition. |
| 3 | **Lean on tackles+assists and passing TDs.** Keep sacks and receiving yards to a minimum. | T+A 9-4 +22%, pass TD 8-3 +14%; rec yds −27%, receptions −18%, sacks 2-3 |
| 4 | **Props go on the side you expect to win.** Never stack an offense you fade elsewhere on the card. | 56% vs 39% (Week 2) |
| 5 | **Each starting QB is one shared risk** across every leg on his offense. Count those legs as one exposure. | MNF Dart injury: Giants legs 4-15 |
| 6 | **ML chalk ≤ −290 is not a free anchor.** Flag it; one per ticket at most. | 6-4 vs ~78% implied; TB −410, BAL −379, LAC −292 all lost |
| 7 | **Structure:** 2-leg tickets and 2-team RRs first. Straight parlays of 5+ legs are moonshots only ($5, one or two a week). | All 3 Week 2 winners were 2-leg or 2-team; 5+ leg straights 0-26 |
| 8 | **Receptions are tight to the line.** Only for proven target share on the expected winner. Yardage is bimodal, so don't pay −110 to −120 for a median line. | 9 of 12 rec losses were within 1.5 catches |
| 9 | **Moonshot ATD stacks lose.** One long-priced TD (+150 or longer) is fine as a single or in an RR. | ATD moonshots 0-11 on scorers; +150-or-longer band +20% |
| 10 | Bookmaker vs BetOnline: **no edge either way** (50% vs 49% after the 9/22 book correction). Choose the book by rule and price, not habit. | — |
